interpretation: Structural validity and traceability do not establish completeness or learner readiness. Higher-level sources, alternate paths, and other source outcomes are inspection signals, not automatic defects. Do not delete edges or split decks without evaluating their contracts.

exclusions.subject: mathematics
exclusions.rationale: Higher categories, derived geometry, large-cardinal research and the Langlands program are not cataloged. Included algebra, geometry, logic and number-theory rows provide their ordinary disciplinary foundations, not these specialties.

exclusions.subject: computer-science
exclusions.rationale: Vendor credentials and exhaustive platform administration are excluded; architecture, networks, security, databases and distributed operation are taught as durable methods.

exclusions.subject: computer-science
exclusions.rationale: Quantum algorithm research, exhaustive AI architectures and specialist language metatheory are outside the representative continuations; no mastery of these specialties is claimed.

exclusions.subject: biology
exclusions.rationale: Clinical, veterinary and therapeutic authorization requires separate professional education; physiology, immunity, disease ecology and experimental decision-making are included independently.

exclusions.subject: biology
exclusions.rationale: Exhaustive taxon-specific and disease-specific research catalogs are excluded, not organism identification, behavior, field methods or molecular mechanisms.

exclusions.subject: chemistry
exclusions.rationale: Chemical-plant engineering certification and pharmaceutical release authority are separate qualifications; process balances, analysis, electrochemistry and synthesis decisions remain included.

exclusions.subject: chemistry
exclusions.rationale: Exhaustive named-reaction and instrument-platform catalogs are excluded; working synthesis, spectroscopy, surface chemistry and structural inference are included.

exclusions.subject: physics
exclusions.domain: Additional frontier theories and engineering qualifications
exclusions.rationale: Quantum gravity, string theory and full reactor or accelerator engineering are outside this progression; nuclear, field, plasma, kinetic and experimental methods are included without claiming those qualifications.

includes: Gene-editing design, quantitative imaging, pooled and arrayed screens, causal validation and biotechnology decisions.

outcomes.description: Design editing and delivery strategies and quantitative imaging assays with independent identity, off-target, specificity and expression controls.
Design powered pooled or arrayed screens, analyze effect estimates and false discoveries and validate hits through independent perturbation and rescue.

practice: Design an approved low-risk reporter or editing study and analyze screen data with independent hit validation.

includes: Animal tissues, transport, neural and endocrine regulation, major organ systems and comparative homeostasis.

outcomes.description: Identify major tissues and organ arrangements and infer circulatory, respiratory, digestive, renal, neural, endocrine and reproductive regulation from perturbation data.
Derive bounded diffusion, pressure-flow, mass-balance and Nernst models algebraically and apply them to transport, potentials and feedback with regime checks.

practice: Analyze dehydration or exercise using quantitative balances and competing organ-system feedback explanations.

includes: Ethograms, behavioral sampling, learning, communication, foraging, mating, sociality and proximate versus evolutionary explanation.

outcomes.description: Compare learning, communication, foraging, mating and social-behavior hypotheses using explicit payoff tables and proximate versus evolutionary evidence.
Construct ethograms and focal or scan sampling protocols and quantify behavior while controlling observer bias and repeated observations.

practice: Analyze a behavioral observation or playback study and design a noninvasive discriminating comparison.

includes: Biological organization, heredity, evolution, major lineages, life cycles and ecosystems at descriptive entry depth.

outcomes.description: Read life-cycle, food-web and branching-tree diagrams and distinguish major microbial, fungal, plant and animal lineages.
Explain simple inheritance and population change through variation, reproduction, selection and chance without purposeful-evolution reasoning.
Compare cells and organismal organization; distinguish observations, functions and mechanistic explanations.

practice: Construct an evidence-annotated explanation at cellular, organismal and population scales.

includes: Membranes, organelles, transport, cytoskeleton, cell cycle, genetic information, signaling and perturbation inference.

outcomes.description: Predict transport, trafficking, cytoskeletal and cell-cycle behavior using molecular organization, gradients and explicitly defined equilibrium binding models.
Represent replication, transcription, RNA processing, translation and signaling and predict molecular perturbation effects on regulation.
Infer mechanisms from localization, inhibition, time-course and rescue evidence while distinguishing direct effects, feedback and alternatives.

practice: Compare competing trafficking or regulatory mechanisms against a perturbation dataset.

includes: Conductance and integrate-and-fire neurons, recurrent networks, spike likelihoods and encoding-model validation.

outcomes.description: Derive membrane current balances and implement Hodgkin-Huxley, integrate-and-fire and recurrent-network models with stability and timestep checks.
Derive discretized Poisson and point-process spike likelihoods and fit encoding models with held-out prediction, time-bin and residual diagnostics.

practice: Compare a mechanistic spiking model and fitted encoding model against neural recordings.

includes: Extinction risk, fragmentation, conservation genetics, restoration, monitoring and management decisions.

outcomes.description: Assess vulnerability from demographic, connectivity and genetic evidence and construct bounded population projections and restoration monitoring designs.
Compare uncertain outcomes, costs, equity and ecological objectives and justify adaptive management while addressing local and Indigenous knowledge obligations.

practice: Prepare a conservation dossier with alternatives, sensitivity analysis, stakeholder obligations and measurable monitoring rules.

includes: Fertilization, axes, induction, differentiation, morphogenesis, regeneration and developmental inference.

outcomes.description: Infer mechanisms from fate mapping, transplantation, timed perturbation and rescue and distinguish specification, determination and cell autonomy.
Represent lineage, positional information, regulatory interactions and tissue mechanics in axis formation, differentiation and morphogenesis.

practice: Reconstruct a developmental model and propose a timed intervention that distinguishes alternatives.

includes: Transmission routes, reservoirs, discrete epidemic models, reproduction thresholds and outbreak study design.

outcomes.description: Estimate attack rates and risk ratios and compare outbreak hypotheses using sampling, surveillance and contact evidence; justify intervention under uncertainty and equity constraints.
Construct discrete susceptible-infectious-recovered and vector-host updates, derive elementary reproduction thresholds and compare reservoir and contact mechanisms.

practice: Analyze an outbreak dataset and compare interventions using a validated spreadsheet transmission model.

includes: Sampling, life tables, discrete growth, species interactions, diversity, food webs, nutrient cycling and disturbance.

outcomes.description: Calculate diversity and energy or nutrient budgets and evaluate experiments on communities, succession, disturbance and environmental change.
Estimate abundance and survival with quadrats, transects and capture-recapture; construct life tables and discrete population and interaction models.

practice: Design a field sample and estimate population state and disturbance response with uncertainty.

includes: Selection, drift, mutation, migration, mating, speciation, phylogenies and comparative adaptation tests.

outcomes.description: Construct small character phylogenies and evaluate speciation and adaptation against historical, demographic and nonadaptive alternatives.
Calculate Hardy-Weinberg expectations and discrete allele-frequency updates under selection, mutation and migration and distinguish deterministic change from drift.

practice: Analyze allele-frequency and comparative-trait evidence while separating selection and ancestry explanations.

includes: Wright-Fisher dynamics, coalescent genealogies, linkage, selection, demographic inference and phylogenomics.

outcomes.description: Fit bounded demographic and phylogenetic likelihoods and distinguish selection, structure, recombination and sequencing artifacts through simulation and model criticism.
Derive and simulate drift, mutation and selection models and coalescent waiting times and calculate diversity, fixation and linkage summaries.

practice: Infer population history and test whether an apparent selection signal survives demographic alternatives.

includes: Biological study design, sampling, pipetting, microscopy, aseptic handling, image measurement and ethics.

outcomes.description: Design controls, replication, randomization and blinding and distinguish technical replication, biological replication and causal identification.
Compare scientific value, consent, welfare, ecological impact, biosafety and equitable participation and justify a revised protocol.
Perform calibrated dilution, pipetting, microscopy, aseptic handling and image counting with provenance and measurement-error records.

practice: Execute an approved low-risk microscopy study with raw records, controls and an ethics revision.

includes: Mendelian and non-Mendelian inheritance, pedigrees, linkage, quantitative traits and molecular genetic inference.

outcomes.description: Use complementation, epistasis, deletion, expression and rescue to infer gene function and pathway order with penetrance and background checks.
Calculate cross and pedigree probabilities and construct recombination maps; distinguish sex-linked, cytoplasmic, Mendelian and quantitative inheritance.

practice: Infer a map and pathway from crosses and perturbations and design a distinguishing experiment.

includes: Sequence formats, alignment, search, reads, variants, phylogenetic likelihood and omics workflow validation.

outcomes.description: Use reproducible read, variant and expression tools; calculate small-tree likelihoods from explicitly defined substitution probabilities and diagnose batch, multiplicity and reference effects.
Parse sequence formats and implement dynamic-programming pairwise alignment with scores, traceback and cost analysis; compare sequence-search assumptions.

practice: Implement an aligner and validate a variant or expression workflow using independent calls and sensitivity analyses.

includes: Innate and adaptive immunity, recognition, receptor diversification, memory, tolerance, vaccination and immune assays.

outcomes.description: Interpret antibody, flow-cytometric and infection-response assays with gating and specificity controls and compare evasion, vaccination, allergy and autoimmunity explanations.
Trace sensing, antigen presentation, receptor diversification, clonal selection, effector responses, memory and tolerance through cellular interactions.

practice: Infer an immune defect from controlled assay evidence and design a test separating mechanism from assay failure.

includes: Microbial and viral diversity, metabolism, growth, culture, identification, communities and resistance.

outcomes.description: Compare microbial and viral structures and life cycles, calculate growth and viable counts and explain metabolism and horizontal gene transfer.
Combine culture, stains, biochemical and sequence evidence for identification and interpret susceptibility and community data with contamination controls.

practice: Characterize an approved nonpathogenic isolate or supplied records using independent identification evidence.

includes: Nucleic-acid extraction, PCR, gels, sequence confirmation, protein separation, immunoblotting, cloning and reporters.
excludes: High-throughput screen design and clinical procedures.

outcomes.description: Design primers, restriction or assembly cloning and reporter constructs; select transformation, screening and sequence-confirmation steps and diagnose failed controls.
Design and execute extraction, PCR, electrophoresis and immunoblot workflows; interpret standards, loading, negative and specificity controls.

practice: Complete an approved low-risk PCR or cloning workflow with independent identity confirmation and troubleshooting records.

includes: Neural anatomy, membrane and synaptic signals, sensory and motor systems, plasticity and circuit inference.

outcomes.description: Analyze tuning curves and spike summaries and compare recording, lesion and intervention evidence for sensory, motor and behavioral function.
Interpret intracellular and extracellular recordings and circuit diagrams and explain sensory coding, motor organization and plasticity.

practice: Analyze recordings and behavioral perturbations, separating encoding, correlation and causal necessity.

includes: Plant anatomy, reproduction, meristems, hormones, photosynthesis, water and nutrient transport and stress.

outcomes.description: Identify tissues and organs and explain alternation of generations, meristem growth, reproductive development and hormonal coordination.
Define and apply water-potential and gas-exchange balances, explain photosynthetic light and carbon processes and measure resource or stress responses.

practice: Measure growth or gas-exchange responses and distinguish physiological regulation from measurement artifacts.

includes: Structured populations, nonlinear and spatial ecology, observation models, state-space likelihood and predictive validation.

outcomes.description: Construct matrix-population, consumer-resource and spatial-patch models and analyze equilibria, stability and numerically validated trajectories.
Separate process and observation error and fit bounded occupancy and state-space likelihoods with supplied optimization tools and identifiability and predictive checks.

practice: Fit dynamic abundance data and validate forecasts across withheld seasons and observation assumptions.

includes: Protein purification, macromolecular crystallography, cryo-EM reconstruction, NMR restraints, binding and conformational dynamics.

outcomes.description: Validate models using independent reflections, half-maps or restraints and combine binding, mutational and kinetic data to distinguish conformational mechanisms and model bias.
Design purification and sample-quality workflows and explain crystallographic phasing, single-particle cryo-EM reconstruction and NMR restraint modeling using supplied reconstruction tools.

practice: Evaluate a macromolecular structural model against independent reconstruction and functional evidence, including unresolved heterogeneity.

includes: Low-risk regulatory and metabolic circuits, resource burden, design-build-test-learn cycles, stability and containment decisions.

outcomes.description: Design a low-risk regulatory or metabolic circuit, predict dynamics and burden and select parts, host context and measurable performance criteria.
Analyze a design-build-test-learn cycle and justify decisions about model failure, evolutionary stability, containment, dual use and deployment boundaries.

practice: Develop a contained circuit investigation or complete design dossier with quantitative success, failure and containment criteria.

includes: Comparative morphology, major organismal groups, body plans, life cycles, identification keys and elementary classification.

outcomes.description: Code morphological characters, explain homology and convergence and construct small character trees; reconcile classifications with supplied molecular-tree evidence.
Use keys and diagnostic structures to distinguish major protist, fungal, plant and animal groups and compare body plans and reproduction.

practice: Build an annotated specimen or image collection, identification key and defensible character matrix.

includes: Stoichiometry, reaction networks, feedback, stochastic reaction events, sensitivities and parameter identification.

outcomes.description: Fit time-course and perturbation parameters, calculate sensitivities and assess structural and practical identifiability to design discriminating measurements.
Construct stoichiometric matrices and mass-action or enzyme-rate ODEs, analyze conservation and stability and implement exact reaction-event sampling for small networks.

practice: Fit deterministic and reaction-event feedback models and choose a perturbation that separates mechanisms.

includes: Chemical group theory, character tables, symmetry-adapted orbitals, ligand-field states, magnetism and inorganic electronic inference.

outcomes.description: Construct ligand-field term and spin models and combine electronic spectra, magnetic and structural evidence to discriminate bonding and oxidation-state assignments.
Construct finite symmetry representations and reduce them with character orthogonality; derive projection operators and symmetry-adapted orbitals and vibrational selections.

practice: Analyze a coordination complex with explicit symmetry reduction and competing electronic-structure assignments.

includes: Integrated functional-material design, processing, molecular computation and structural and performance validation.

outcomes.description: Formulate a testable structure-property hypothesis and select synthesis, processing and computation for a bounded functional-material target.
Design complementary characterization and performance tests and justify go-or-no-go decisions considering mechanism, reproducibility, degradation, scale and lifecycle constraints.

practice: Test a materials hypothesis using a small computation and independent characterization and performance evidence.

includes: Molecular partition functions, fluctuations, transition-state theory, kinetic master equations and relaxation correlations.

outcomes.description: Construct translational, rotational, vibrational and electronic partition functions and derive equilibrium constants and heat capacities with symmetry and standard-state corrections.
Derive transition-state and activated-rate models and finite-state master equations and relate relaxation modes and time correlations to chemical measurements.

practice: Predict equilibrium and rate changes from molecular models and test transient relaxation against mechanism constraints.

includes: Multidimensional NMR, tandem MS, diffraction, time-resolved spectroscopy, response convolution and inverse fitting.

outcomes.description: Construct instrument-convolved kinetic spectral models and implement bounded nonlinear least-squares fitting with sensitivity, uncertainty and alternative-model tests.
Interpret two-dimensional NMR and tandem-MS constraints, derive diffraction structure factors and combine restraints with resolution and ambiguity checks.

practice: Infer structure and relaxation mechanisms from complementary data, including simulated ambiguities and response effects.

includes: Quantitative assays, analytical equilibria, calibration, detection limits, electroanalysis, absorption and chromatography.

outcomes.description: Design gravimetric, titrimetric and calibrated assays using mass and charge balances and quantify detection limits, uncertainty, recovery and matrix effects.
Explain and operate bounded potentiometric, voltammetric, absorption and chromatographic methods and diagnose response and separation efficiency.

practice: Develop a mixture assay using standards, spikes, blanks and an independently checked separation.

includes: Biomolecular structure, folding, binding, enzyme kinetics, biochemical energetics and central metabolism.

outcomes.description: Relate protein, lipid, carbohydrate and nucleic-acid structures to function; derive steady-state Michaelis-Menten kinetics algebraically and distinguish inhibition from rate data.
Trace atoms, electrons and ATP through central catabolic and anabolic pathways and calculate coupled energy and redox balances and regulatory effects.

practice: Analyze enzyme-rate and isotope-labeling evidence with explicit kinetic and balance checks.

includes: Moles, stoichiometry, solutions, atomic structure, bonding and molecular geometry.

outcomes.description: Balance equations and calculate moles, concentrations, composition and limiting reagents with units and significant figures.
Use electron configurations, periodicity, Lewis structures, resonance and three-dimensional geometry to predict bonding, polarity and intermolecular interactions.

practice: Infer composition from mass data and compare structural explanations of physical properties.

includes: Operational IR, UV-visible, mass spectrometry and one-dimensional NMR models and structure elucidation.
excludes: Quantum derivations and advanced multidimensional methods.

outcomes.description: Rank structures from formulas and complementary IR, mass and NMR evidence; assign signals and propose discriminating measurements.
Explain vibration, absorption, fragmentation and spin-resonance models; interpret spectral axes, isotope patterns, shifts, integration and splitting, including calibration and resolution limitations.

practice: Solve blinded structure cases and document assignments, ambiguities and confirming experiments.

includes: Electronic workflows, self-consistency, geometry optimization, force fields, molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo validation.

outcomes.description: Implement a small SCF calculation from supplied integrals and use packages for geometry and energies with basis, spin, method and convergence checks.
Implement pair forces, Verlet dynamics and Metropolis sampling and assess ensemble control, energy drift, equilibration, autocorrelation and finite-size effects.

practice: Compare molecular electronic calculations and fluid simulations while separating implemented methods from package capabilities.

includes: Electrode interfaces, charge transfer, diffusion, potentiostats, voltammetry, impedance, batteries and corrosion.

outcomes.description: Interpret voltammetry and impedance using explicitly derived resistor-capacitor and diffusion responses and discriminate kinetic, transport and degradation mechanisms.
Derive Butler-Volmer and Tafel limits and bounded planar diffusion-current models and explain reference electrodes, potentiostatic control and double-layer charging.

practice: Fit controlled electrode data and compare battery or corrosion explanations with rate and transport checks.

includes: Air, water and soil chemistry, sampling, speciation, compartment transport, process balances and sustainability.

outcomes.description: Design sampling and assays, calculate speciation and implement spreadsheet compartment updates from transfer and reaction rates with mass-balance and timestep checks.
Construct process mass and energy inventories and compare treatment and remediation using exposure, waste, uncertainty and bounded lifecycle evidence.

practice: Analyze a contaminant release using measurements, a dynamic compartment model and a justified intervention.

includes: Main-group chemistry, symmetry operations, coordination geometry, ligand fields, orbital models and crystal structures.

outcomes.description: Classify symmetry and coordination geometry and construct qualitative orbital and ligand-field diagrams to predict bonding, color and magnetism.
Compare coordination substitution and redox pathways and calculate unit-cell composition and structural implications for ionic, metallic and network solids.

practice: Identify a coordination compound from magnetic, structural and reaction evidence.

includes: Solutions, balances, volumetric tools, extraction, filtration, distillation, titration, notebooks and risk decisions.

outcomes.description: Prepare and standardize solutions and execute separations and titrations with reproducible records, recoveries and uncertainty estimates.
Use blanks, replicates and calibration checks to diagnose errors and justify procedures by comparing exposure, waste, substitution and hazard controls.

practice: Standardize a solution and separate a mixture with an uncertainty budget and approved risk assessment.

includes: Polymerization, molecular-weight distributions, polymer architecture, ceramics, metals, composites and processing-property relations.

outcomes.description: Compare chain and step polymerization, calculate molecular-weight averages and ideal conversion relations and classify crystalline, amorphous and composite structures.
Interpret stress-strain, thermal and electrical measurements and justify processing and material selection using degradation, performance and lifecycle evidence.

practice: Compare candidate materials using synthesis, molecular-weight, mechanical and end-of-life evidence.

includes: Organic representations, conformations, stereochemistry, acidity and principal functional-group mechanisms.

outcomes.description: Construct curved-arrow substitution, elimination, addition, aromatic and carbonyl mechanisms and predict products, rates and selectivity.
Translate line, Newman, chair and wedge-dash structures; assign stereochemistry and compare conformational, resonance and acid-base stability.

practice: Discriminate mechanisms using stereochemical, kinetic and product evidence.

includes: Retrosynthesis, carbon-carbon bond formation, redox, protecting groups, pericyclic reactions and stereoselective synthesis.

outcomes.description: Construct retrosynthetic and forward routes using enolate, organometallic, coupling, redox and pericyclic transformations with compatible conditions.
Predict chemo-, regio- and stereoselectivity and compare routes by yield, purification, step economy, hazards and required product evidence.

practice: Defend two routes to a stereodefined target against likely side reactions and practical constraints.

includes: Reaction-coordinate models, substituent effects, isotope effects, stereoelectronic reasoning and mechanistic experiments.

outcomes.description: Combine kinetics, labeling, crossover, stereochemical and spectroscopic evidence to distinguish concerted, ionic and radical pathways and identify confounded tests.
Construct free-energy profiles and linear free-energy relationships and predict solvent, substituent and isotope effects with competing mechanistic assumptions.

practice: Design a mechanism-discrimination program and analyze a case with contradictory kinetic and labeling evidence.

includes: Born-Oppenheimer separation, molecular orbitals, antisymmetry, Hartree-Fock, correlation limits and molecular spectra.

outcomes.description: Apply Born-Oppenheimer separation, construct orbitals and antisymmetric Slater determinants and derive finite-basis Hartree-Fock equations and correlation limitations.
Use symmetry and transition moments to calculate rotational-vibrational spectra and relate potential-energy surfaces to bonding and reaction coordinates.

practice: Construct a small molecular-orbital calculation and predict isotope and geometry-dependent spectra.

includes: Gas and solution models, calorimetry, equilibrium, acids, solubility, redox cells and introductory rates.

outcomes.description: Solve acid-base, buffer, solubility and redox-cell problems and infer simple rate laws and Arrhenius parameters from data.
Use gas laws, calorimetric balances, reaction quotients and equilibrium constants to calculate composition and direction, including bounded Gibbs-energy relations.

practice: Analyze titration, cell and rate datasets with mass-balance, charge-balance and approximation checks.

includes: Surface free energy, adsorption, wetting, micelles, colloidal forces, aggregation and characterization.

outcomes.description: Calculate micellization and explicitly defined electrostatic-attraction colloid models and interpret size, scattering and aggregation measurements with polydispersity limitations.
Derive bounded adsorption isotherms and capillary and wetting relations and infer surface area or adsorption mechanisms from controlled data.

practice: Compare dispersion stability under salt or surfactant changes using adsorption and particle-size evidence.

includes: Organometallic steps, homogeneous and surface catalysis, asymmetric synthesis, deactivation and process-aware mechanism testing.

outcomes.description: Construct catalytic cycles using electron counting, ligands and elementary steps and compare homogeneous, surface-site and asymmetric strategies.
Derive rate and isotope predictions, interpret resting states and compare turnover, selectivity, deactivation, scale and hazards across competing routes.

practice: Design a catalytic route and a discriminating rate, labeling and resting-state measurement program.

includes: Chemical potentials, activities, phase coexistence, electrochemical thermodynamics, reaction mechanisms and relaxation kinetics.

outcomes.description: Construct coupled rate equations, derive steady-state and pre-equilibrium limits and fit competing transient mechanisms with supplied nonlinear least-squares tools and identifiability checks.
Derive thermodynamic differentials and Maxwell relations and calculate chemical potentials, activities, nonideal phase coexistence and electrochemical equilibria.

practice: Calculate nonideal phase behavior and discriminate kinetic models using concentration and temperature series.

includes: Randomized, approximation and online algorithms, concentration, reductions and lower bounds.

outcomes.description: Design randomized, approximation and online algorithms and prove expectation, concentration, approximation-ratio and competitive guarantees.
Construct reductions and adversarial, counting and communication-style lower bounds and distinguish computational from information limitations.

practice: Pair an implemented algorithm with a complete guarantee and a near-worst-case construction.

includes: Heuristic and adversarial search, constraints, logical representation, inference and classical planning.

outcomes.description: Represent facts and actions logically, implement bounded unification and inference and construct and validate classical plans.
Implement uninformed and heuristic search, minimax pruning and constraint propagation and justify completeness and optimality assumptions.

practice: Build a planner or game agent and compare representations and heuristics through measured failures and search costs.

includes: Combinational and sequential logic, instruction sets, datapaths, pipelines, caches and performance.

outcomes.description: Design arithmetic circuits, finite-state controllers and a small instruction-set datapath in a logic simulator.
Analyze pipeline hazards, cache mappings and memory locality and compare predicted and measured execution costs.

practice: Build a simulated processor and compare cache and pipeline configurations on identical traces.

includes: Meshes, homogeneous coordinates, projection, rasterization, local illumination, ray tracing, sampling and animation.

outcomes.description: Represent spatial meshes and implement camera transforms, clipping, rasterization and depth buffering using homogeneous coordinates.
Implement explicitly defined local illumination and basic ray tracing, diagnose aliasing and animate objects using rigid transforms and polynomial spline interpolation.

practice: Render the same scene by rasterization and ray tracing and compare visibility, lighting approximations and sampling artifacts.

includes: Bits, Boolean logic, integer and floating-point encoding, instructions, stack, heap, processes and permissions.

outcomes.description: Trace instructions, calls and stack or heap memory and relate executables to processes, files and permissions.
Encode numbers and characters, evaluate Boolean circuits and explain overflow, precision loss and representation boundaries.

practice: Inspect a compiled program and diagnose an instruction, memory or representation bug.

includes: Image filtering, edges, segmentation, feature matching, pinhole cameras, calibration and triangulation.

outcomes.description: Derive pinhole projection and homogeneous camera equations; implement linear calibration, robust correspondence sampling and triangulation with reprojection-error checks.
Implement image convolution, gradients, threshold and clustering segmentation and feature matching; diagnose noise, scale and illumination sensitivity.

practice: Recover a small scene from calibrated images and validate geometry using withheld correspondences.

includes: Symmetric and public-key primitives, signatures, key exchange, security games and elementary reductions.

outcomes.description: Implement educational modular encryption, signatures and key exchange and explain pseudorandomness, modes, hashes and message authentication.
Formulate indistinguishability and unforgeability games, construct attacks and elementary reductions and analyze composition and key-management assumptions.

practice: Break flawed constructions, prove a bounded reduction and distinguish educational code from production cryptography.

includes: Lists, hashing, trees, heaps, graphs, algorithmic paradigms, correctness and asymptotic complexity.

outcomes.description: Implement sorting, traversal, shortest paths and representative greedy, divide-and-conquer and dynamic-programming algorithms.
Prove correctness through invariants and induction and analyze worst-case, amortized and recurrence-based time and space costs.
Implement linked structures, hash tables, balanced-tree operations, heaps and graph representations while preserving invariants.

practice: Build a route-planning library with correctness tests and measured complexity comparisons.

includes: Relational models, SQL, normalization, query execution, indexing, transactions and nonrelational tradeoffs.

outcomes.description: Design normalized schemas and write relational-algebra and SQL queries with constraints, dependencies and null semantics.
Explain index and join execution, inspect plans and reason about serializability, isolation and logging; compare document and key-value models.

practice: Build a transactional application, tune a slow query and reproduce then prevent an isolation anomaly.

includes: Distributed failure models, clocks, replication, consistency, consensus, recovery and service operation.

outcomes.description: Implement a bounded replicated-log consensus protocol, prove safety invariants and analyze impossibility, liveness and operational failure limits.
Specify happens-before relations and consistency models and implement replicated storage with explicit partitions, retries, idempotence and recovery behavior.

practice: Operate a replicated service under injected partitions and crashes and report consistency and recovery evidence.

includes: Hoare logic, invariants, weakest preconditions, temporal logic, transition systems and model checking.

outcomes.description: Derive weakest preconditions and loop invariants and construct Hoare proofs tied to an operational semantics.
Specify safety and liveness, implement explicit-state temporal model checking and use supplied SMT tools while assessing abstraction and state-space limits.

practice: Verify a loop and a concurrent protocol and compare proofs, counterexamples and tests.

includes: User research, task analysis, accessible prototyping, usability studies and participatory professional judgment.

outcomes.description: Conduct bounded interviews or observations, analyze tasks and construct paper or interactive prototypes with accessibility criteria.
Evaluate usability with qualitative and quantitative evidence and justify decisions involving consent, exclusion, manipulation and competing stakeholder needs.

practice: Iterate a prototype using approved research or supplied study records and document evidence-driven changes.

includes: Text representation, inverted indexes, ranking, relevance evaluation, smoothed language models and sequence tagging.

outcomes.description: Estimate smoothed n-gram and hidden-state sequence models, implement Viterbi decoding and assess ambiguity, language variation and dataset bias.
Implement tokenization, inverted indexing and TF-IDF or BM25 ranking; evaluate relevance with precision, recall and ranked retrieval metrics.

practice: Build a search engine and sequence tagger with held-out evaluation and error analysis across language varieties.

includes: Operational semantics, type systems, paradigms, parsing, intermediate representations and code generation.

outcomes.description: Implement lexing, parsing, name resolution, type checking, intermediate-code optimization and code generation for a small language.
Define evaluation rules, environments and stores; compare paradigms and derive typing judgments and elementary progress and preservation arguments.

practice: Implement matching interpreter and compiler semantics and test rejected programs and optimization correctness.

includes: Regression, neighbors, trees, clustering, PCA, regularization, gradient training and deployment evaluation.

outcomes.description: Build leakage-resistant validation, diagnose overfitting and imbalance and assess predictive uncertainty and subgroup harms in a deployment decision.
Implement linear and logistic regression with explicitly derived component gradients, neighbors, trees, k-means and PCA; explain objectives and regularization.

practice: Implement baselines and compare library models with leakage checks, uncertainty and a deployment recommendation.

includes: Packet networks, addressing, routing, reliability, congestion, sockets, naming and web protocols.

outcomes.description: Trace encapsulation, addressing and routing and calculate latency, throughput and bandwidth-delay effects; implement a routing simulation.
Implement socket applications and bounded reliable transport; diagnose retransmission, congestion, naming and application failures from packet traces.

practice: Build a client-server service and diagnose injected loss, delay and naming faults.

includes: Computational graphs, backpropagation, basic neural models and finite Markov decision learning.
excludes: Generalization theory and general approximate Bayesian inference.

outcomes.description: Define finite MDP transition and reward tables, derive Bellman recursions and implement value iteration and tabular Q-learning with separate evaluation trajectories.
Derive scalar-node chain rules and implement backpropagation, minibatch training and a small dense or convolutional network with gradient checks.

practice: Train a small neural predictor and a tabular agent, documenting optimization, exploration and generalization failures.

includes: Processes, scheduling, synchronization, virtual memory, files, protection and crash recovery.

outcomes.description: Implement scheduling and thread synchronization with locks and condition variables; diagnose races, deadlock and starvation.
Trace address translation and page replacement and construct file-system and recovery models with protection and persistence invariants.

practice: Build a concurrent service and a simulated memory or file-system component with adversarial schedules and crash tests.

includes: Shared-memory and message-passing programming, decomposition, synchronization and scaling.

outcomes.description: Implement task and data parallelism with threads and message-passing processes; preserve synchronization and ownership invariants.
Analyze work, span, Amdahl bounds, communication, load imbalance and locality and measure strong and weak scaling.

practice: Parallelize a matrix or graph workload and explain scaling limits from measured resource costs.

includes: Control flow, collections, functions, recursion, objects, files, debugging and tests in one general-purpose language.

outcomes.description: Represent problems using lists, maps and records; use recursion, higher-order functions and simple objects to separate concerns.
Write and trace programs using variables, conditionals, loops, functions and file input/output.
Debug execution and logic errors and implement boundary-case and property-based tests.

practice: Implement a data-cleaning application with malformed-input handling, automated tests and reproducible reports.

includes: Robot transforms, kinematics, Jacobians, Bayesian localization, occupancy maps and configuration-space planning.

outcomes.description: Calculate rigid transforms, forward and inverse kinematics and manipulator Jacobians; derive discrete planar mobile-robot motion models.
Implement discrete Bayes and linear-Gaussian Kalman localization, occupancy updates and configuration-space planning with uncertainty and collision checks.

practice: Implement a simulated robot that localizes from noisy landmarks and plans a collision-free route.

includes: Threat modeling, memory and web failures, authentication, access control, secure library use and authorized assessment.

outcomes.description: Plan authorized assessments, validate fixes and interpret incident evidence; justify disclosure, privacy and residual-risk decisions.
Threat-model systems and demonstrate memory, injection, authentication and protocol-use failures in isolation; implement least-privilege and established-library defenses.

practice: Assess a deliberately vulnerable local application and deliver reproducible fixes and a risk-ranked report.

includes: Requirements, interfaces, version control, review, testing, continuous integration, maintenance and professional obligations.

outcomes.description: Assess quality using contracts and unit, integration and property tests; justify reliability, accessibility, privacy, licensing and stakeholder-harm decisions.
Elicit requirements, design modules and interfaces and maintain reviewed version-controlled builds, tests and releases.

practice: Complete a team project with traceable requirements, a maintenance change and a documented ethics decision.

includes: Generalization theory, latent-variable inference, attention and sequence architectures, policy gradients and approximation limits.

outcomes.description: Implement attention-based sequence learning and basic policy-gradient estimation; derive objectives and evaluate sequence leakage and off-policy limitations.
Derive and implement EM and variational latent-variable objectives and diagnose nonidentifiability, local optima and approximation bias.
Derive finite-class and capacity-based generalization bounds using explicitly proved concentration inequalities and separate estimation, approximation and optimization errors.

practice: Reproduce bounded latent, sequence and policy-learning experiments with objective derivations, ablations and uncertainty.

includes: Automata, regular expressions, grammars, pushdown machines, Turing computation, reductions and NP-completeness.

outcomes.description: Construct Turing-machine and reduction arguments; prove undecidability, NP membership and NP-completeness for explicit decision problems.
Construct and transform finite automata, regular expressions, context-free grammars and pushdown recognizers and prove selected language impossibility results.

practice: Provide a recognizer, a language-separation proof and a polynomial reduction with both directions justified.

includes: Differential privacy, private optimization, adversarial robustness, distribution shift and auditing.

outcomes.description: Derive Laplace and Gaussian mechanism conditions and basic composition and implement clipped noisy-gradient learning with an explicit privacy budget.
Construct adversarial and distribution-shift evaluations and justify an audit decision distinguishing empirical robustness, formal guarantees, utility and subgroup harms.

practice: Audit a private learner against explicit neighboring-data and adversary definitions, including negative findings.

includes: Groups, actions, homomorphisms, rings, ideals, fields and quotients.

outcomes.description: Construct groups, quotients and actions; prove isomorphism, orbit-stabilizer and Sylow results and apply them to finite groups.
Calculate ideals, quotient rings and polynomial factorizations; prove basic ring and field results and construct finite extensions.

practice: Classify small examples and prove when explicit quotients are fields.

includes: Affine and projective varieties, coordinate rings, morphisms, dimension, singularities and affine schemes.

outcomes.description: Use local rings, formal derivatives, dimension and tangent spaces to detect singularities and interpret prime spectra and regular functions.
Relate ideals and varieties through the Nullstellensatz and construct coordinate rings and affine or projective morphisms.

practice: Analyze a curve through its equations, local singularities and projective completion.

includes: Number fields, algebraic integers, ideals, ramification, units and class groups.

outcomes.description: Analyze ramification, units and ideal classes in quadratic examples; prove ideal-factorization results and apply geometric lattice bounds.
Compute integral bases, norms, traces and discriminants and factor prime ideals in explicit number fields.

practice: Compute a quadratic field's arithmetic invariants and explain failure of element factorization.

includes: Homotopy, fundamental groups, coverings, chain complexes, simplicial and singular homology and exact sequences.

outcomes.description: Compute fundamental groups with van Kampen and analyze covering spaces, lifting and homotopy properties.
Construct chain complexes and compute homology using boundary matrices and exact sequences; prove obstructions to maps and deformations.

practice: Distinguish cell-built spaces using independently computed fundamental groups and homology.

includes: Arithmetic sums, Dirichlet series, Euler products, zeta and L-functions and introductory prime-distribution arguments.

outcomes.description: Transform arithmetic sums using convolution and partial summation and derive convergence and Euler products of Dirichlet series.
Analyze zeta and Dirichlet L-functions through continuation and characters; prove elementary prime-distribution bounds and a bounded progression theorem.

practice: Derive an arithmetic asymptotic with a justified error bound and compare numerical evidence.

includes: One-variable limits, derivatives, integrals, Taylor approximation and series.

outcomes.description: Evaluate limits and derivatives and solve optimization and related-rate problems with local interpretations and domain checks.
Evaluate definite and improper integrals; apply substitution, integration by parts, the fundamental theorem, series tests and Taylor error estimates.

practice: Analyze a growth or motion model and bound the error of an approximation.

includes: Proofs of Cauchy theory, analytic continuation, argument principle, normal limits and conformal theory.

outcomes.description: Prove Cauchy's theorem, integral formula, identity and maximum principles with precise topological and regularity hypotheses.
Use analytic continuation, the argument principle and locally uniform convergence to prove zero-counting, mapping and meromorphic-function results.

practice: Prove a zero-counting or continuation result and justify every limiting contour operation.

includes: Complex differentiation, contour parameterization, Cauchy formulas, Laurent series, residues and elementary conformal maps.
excludes: Global analytic proofs are taught in Complex Analysis.

outcomes.description: Calculate complex derivatives and contour integrals; derive Cauchy-Riemann equations using component derivatives and apply Cauchy formulas under stated hypotheses.
Compute Laurent expansions and residues, evaluate real integrals with explicit arc bounds, and construct elementary conformal maps with branch choices.

practice: Evaluate a real integral by residues and map a simple planar boundary domain.

includes: Finite-matrix inverse models, SVD filtering, Tikhonov reconstruction and validation.

outcomes.description: Construct forward matrices and implement truncated-SVD and quadratic Tikhonov reconstruction using supplied decompositions; derive the normal equations and spectral filters.
Select regularization using held-out or discrepancy criteria; assess resolution, noise amplification and uncertainty with synthetic recovery and bootstrap experiments.

practice: Reconstruct a one-dimensional blurred signal and report failures under noise and forward-model mismatch.

includes: Parameterized curves and surfaces, curvature, fundamental forms, geodesics and intrinsic geometry.

outcomes.description: Compute arc length, Frenet frames, curvature and torsion for space curves and fundamental forms for parameterized surfaces.
Calculate Gaussian curvature and geodesic equations and verify intrinsic curvature identities on explicit surfaces.

practice: Compare local distances, geodesics and curvature on a plane, cylinder and sphere.

includes: Descriptive statistics, elementary probability, study design, intervals, tests, resampling, regression and multiplicity without calculus.

outcomes.description: Summarize distributions, calculate conditional probabilities and Bayes updates, and distinguish sampling, randomization, confounding and measurement bias.
Calculate intervals and tests for means and proportions; use supplied permutation and bootstrap tools and check assumptions.
Fit and diagnose multiple linear regression with supplied tools; distinguish association from causation and apply familywise and Benjamini-Hochberg controls.

practice: Analyze experimental and observational data with effect sizes, uncertainty, residuals and causal limitations.

includes: First-order and linear higher-order ODEs, forcing, Laplace transforms, matrix systems and local stability.

outcomes.description: Solve separable, first-order linear and constant-coefficient forced equations using integrating factors, characteristic roots and Laplace transforms.
Solve matrix systems and analyze phase portraits; compute linearizations using explicitly taught component partial derivatives and state existence and uniqueness conditions.

practice: Analyze coupled compartments and a forced oscillator, separating transient and steady behavior.

includes: Smooth manifolds, inverse and implicit function theorems, tensors, differential forms, metrics, connections and curvature.

outcomes.description: Transform tensors and calculate metric connections, geodesics, Riemann and Ricci curvature; prove invariance in Riemannian and pseudo-Riemannian examples.
Establish inverse and implicit function tools; construct charts, tangent maps and differential forms and apply manifold integration and Stokes' theorem.

practice: Compute curvature in overlapping charts and verify agreement of geometric observables.

includes: Counting, recurrences, formal generating functions, graphs, matching, flows and extremal arguments.

outcomes.description: Solve enumeration problems using bijections, inclusion-exclusion, recurrences and formal generating functions, with proofs.
Analyze trees, connectivity, planarity, matching and flows; execute constructive methods and prove elementary extremal and graph results.

practice: Construct a matching or flow and prove optimality using a certificate.

includes: Discrete maps, nonlinear flows, bifurcations, limit cycles, Poincare maps and computational chaos diagnostics.

outcomes.description: Analyze fixed points and periodic orbits of maps and planar flows; derive local saddle-node, pitchfork and Hopf normal-form behavior.
Construct Poincare maps and numerical Lyapunov estimates; distinguish chaos, quasiperiodicity, transient effects and discretization artifacts.

practice: Produce a bifurcation study with continuation, phase portraits and numerical convergence checks.

includes: Euclidean constructions, congruence, similarity, circle geometry and elementary geometric proof.

outcomes.description: Construct perpendiculars, angle bisectors, tangents and triangle centers with compass and straightedge; prove correctness and existence conditions.
Prove congruence, similarity, circle-angle and area relations using synthetic and coordinate arguments; distinguish drawings from proofs.

practice: Give two proofs of a geometric claim and construct a configuration satisfying specified constraints.

includes: Banach and Hilbert spaces, duality, bounded and compact operators, weak convergence and variational equations.

outcomes.description: Analyze compact self-adjoint spectra and weak convergence; construct elementary Sobolev spaces and prove existence for coercive variational equations.
Prove completeness and duality results and apply Hahn-Banach, uniform boundedness and open-mapping principles to function spaces.

practice: Prove existence for a one-dimensional weak boundary problem and compare finite-dimensional spectral approximations.

includes: Galois theory, modules, exact sequences, tensor products, Noetherian rings, localization and finite-group representations.

outcomes.description: Compute splitting fields and Galois groups and apply the Galois correspondence to extension and solvability problems.
Construct modules, exact sequences and tensor products and prove results about Noetherian rings, prime ideals and localization.
Decompose complex finite-group representations using invariant subspaces, characters and orthogonality relations.

practice: Compute a Galois correspondence, a localization and a character decomposition.

includes: Distributions, Sobolev weak PDEs, elliptic and parabolic existence, finite elements and error analysis.

outcomes.description: Implement piecewise-linear finite elements for one- and two-dimensional Poisson problems, derive Galerkin error bounds and verify mesh convergence.
Define distributional derivatives and traces; prove weak elliptic and parabolic existence and energy estimates using coercivity and Galerkin approximation.

practice: Prove a weak-solution estimate and implement a triangular-mesh solution with boundary and convergence tests.

includes: Hierarchical models, missingness, causal identification, Monte Carlo inference and posterior diagnostics.

outcomes.description: Derive hierarchical and mixed-effects likelihoods; analyze missing-data assumptions and causal identification with potential outcomes and directed graphs.
Implement importance sampling, Metropolis-Hastings and Gibbs sampling; diagnose mixing and Monte Carlo error and conduct posterior predictive and sensitivity checks.

practice: Fit a hierarchical study model and compare missingness and causal assumptions through explicit sensitivity analyses.

includes: Compact forward operators, ill-posedness, regularization convergence and finite-dimensional Bayesian inversion.

outcomes.description: Prove nonuniqueness or instability using operator spectra and distinguish continuum ill-posedness from discretization error.
Derive spectral and variational regularization convergence conditions and compare parameter-choice rules and Bayesian uncertainty under model mismatch.

practice: Prove a reconstruction stability statement and test its limitations in a spatial inverse problem.

includes: Systems, vector spaces, bases, linear maps, inner products, least squares, eigenvalues and singular values.

outcomes.description: Solve systems by elimination and represent linear maps using bases, matrices, rank, null spaces and determinants.
Compute projections, least-squares solutions, eigenvectors and SVDs; interpret real or complex inner products, diagonalization and positive quadratic forms.

practice: Recover parameters from an overdetermined system and diagnose near-dependence and residual error.

includes: First-order syntax, semantics, proof systems, completeness, compactness and arithmetic incompleteness.

outcomes.description: Encode syntax arithmetically and derive incompleteness and undecidability arguments while distinguishing consistency, soundness and representability assumptions.
Construct structures and derivations, prove soundness and completeness through a model construction and apply compactness.

practice: Construct a compactness proof and a detailed arithmetic diagonalization argument.

includes: Likelihood, sufficiency, information, asymptotic inference, generalized linear models, Bayesian inference and decision theory.

outcomes.description: Compare estimators by loss and risk; derive conjugate updates and posterior predictions and assess prior sensitivity and coverage.
Derive estimators, sufficient statistics, information and likelihood-ratio tests; assess identifiability, consistency and asymptotic uncertainty, including generalized linear models.

practice: Derive likelihood and Bayesian analyses for count data, including a nonidentifiable alternative.

includes: Sigma-algebras, measure construction, Lebesgue integration, product measures and Radon-Nikodym derivatives.

outcomes.description: Prove and apply monotone and dominated convergence, Fatou, Fubini-Tonelli and Radon-Nikodym results with counterexamples to missing hypotheses.
Construct measures from outer measures and define and calculate Lebesgue integrals, measurable sets and null sets.

practice: Justify a sequence of limit and integral interchanges and construct failure examples.

includes: Multivariable derivatives, constrained extrema, coordinate changes and vector integral theorems.

outcomes.description: Calculate gradients, Jacobians, Hessians, multivariable chain rules, Taylor expansions and constrained extrema.
Evaluate multiple, line and surface integrals in Cartesian, cylindrical and spherical coordinates; apply Green, divergence and Stokes theorems.

practice: Compute curved-surface flux directly and through a volume theorem, checking orientations and hypotheses.

includes: Divisibility, factorization, arithmetic functions, Diophantine equations, congruences and quadratic residues.

outcomes.description: Solve modular systems using Chinese remaindering and modular powers; analyze quadratic residues and prove selected reciprocity consequences.
Use the Euclidean algorithm and unique factorization to solve divisibility and linear Diophantine problems and calculate arithmetic functions.

practice: Construct complete modular solution sets and expose failures of plausible primality tests.

includes: ODE integration, convergence and stability analysis, stiffness and adaptive error control.

outcomes.description: Derive consistency and linear absolute-stability results, explain global-error propagation and diagnose stiffness and conservation drift.
Implement Euler, Runge-Kutta and elementary implicit methods with step control; compare trajectories with exact or refined solutions.

practice: Compare explicit and implicit solvers on stiff and nonstiff systems with convergence evidence.

includes: Floating-point error, conditioning, linear and scalar nonlinear solvers, interpolation and quadrature.

outcomes.description: Implement interpolation and quadrature; derive elementary Taylor-based error orders and measure approximation-roundoff tradeoffs.
Implement pivoted elimination, iterative linear solution, power iteration and bracketed or Newton root finding; diagnose conditioning, residuals and floating-point error.

practice: Build a tested solver and quadrature library with convergence and conditioning studies.

includes: Linear, convex and integer optimization, duality, constrained optimality and computational methods.

outcomes.description: Implement gradient, projected-gradient and Newton methods; execute simplex and branch-and-bound and assess convergence, certificates and optimality gaps.
Formulate linear, convex and integer programs; prove elementary convexity results and derive duals and KKT conditions with constraint qualifications.

practice: Solve constrained estimation and allocation problems with sensitivity analysis and certificates or gaps.

includes: Transport, heat, wave and Laplace equations; characteristics, Fourier expansions, boundary methods and energy estimates.

outcomes.description: Construct Fourier series and transforms and eigenfunction expansions for heat, wave and potential problems on intervals, rectangles and radial domains.
Derive PDEs from conservation laws, classify canonical types, solve first-order transport by characteristics and prove elementary energy-based uniqueness estimates.

practice: Compare heat and wave evolution for the same initial profile and explicit boundary conditions.

includes: Discrete and continuous probability, bivariate laws, transformations, expectation and introductory limit results.

outcomes.description: Calculate joint and conditional laws using explicitly taught iterated double integrals, convolution and covariance; prove elementary inequalities and justify LLN and CLT approximations.
Construct probability models and calculate conditional probabilities, expectations, variances and one-variable transformed densities.

practice: Derive a sum distribution and compare exact tail probabilities with a limit approximation.

includes: Logic, sets, relations, maps, countability and standard proof methods.

outcomes.description: Translate quantifiers and use sets, functions, equivalence relations, quotient sets and finite or countable cardinalities precisely.
Construct direct, contrapositive, contradiction and induction proofs; produce counterexamples and diagnose invalid arguments.

practice: Write and revise proofs about divisibility, functions, sums and countability.

includes: Arithmetic, algebra, functions, coordinates, vectors, trigonometry, complex arithmetic, units and graphs.

outcomes.description: Solve linear and quadratic equations; manipulate powers, logarithms and function compositions with domain checks.
Calculate lengths, angles and vector components in two and three dimensions using Cartesian coordinates, trigonometry and complex arithmetic.
Convert units, check dimensions and interpret slopes, areas and linear or logarithmic graphs.

practice: Solve scale, exponential-change and vector-model problems with dimensional and graphical checks.

includes: Completeness, metric limits, compactness, rigorous differentiation, Riemann integration and function convergence.

outcomes.description: Prove differentiation and Riemann-integration results and determine when pointwise or uniform limits commute with continuity, derivatives and integrals.
Prove completeness, sequence, continuity and compactness results using epsilon arguments and metric examples.

practice: Prove a convergence theorem, construct a counterexample and repair the failed hypotheses.

includes: Finite Markov chains, Poisson processes, elementary queues and stochastic simulation.

outcomes.description: Compute finite-chain transition, stationary and absorption probabilities; derive Poisson and exponential waiting-time models and elementary birth-death queue balances.
Implement inverse-transform and categorical sampling, discrete-event simulation and finite-state Metropolis sampling; check stationarity, detailed balance and Monte Carlo error.

practice: Compare analytic queue or absorption predictions with event-driven simulations and uncertainty estimates.

includes: Conditional expectation, filtrations, martingales, Brownian motion, Ito integration and diffusion generators.

outcomes.description: Construct Brownian and Ito models, apply Ito's formula and derive generator, forward and backward equations for diffusion observables.
Construct conditional expectation and filtrations and prove basic martingale convergence and stopping results with hypothesis checks.

practice: Derive hitting probabilities and passage times using stopping arguments and generator equations.

includes: Topological spaces, bases, products, quotients, continuity, compactness, connectedness and separation.

outcomes.description: Prove or refute compactness, connectedness and separation properties and use invariants to distinguish spaces and constrain maps.
Construct spaces from bases, subspaces, products and quotients and compare metric and topological continuity.

practice: Analyze a quotient construction and prove which properties survive.

includes: Radiative transfer, stellar structure, degenerate matter, accretion and quantitative cosmological inference.
excludes: General relativistic field derivations remain in General Relativity.

outcomes.description: Fit expansion and structure-growth data using explicitly stated FLRW and linear-growth equations and assess selection, parameter degeneracy and predictive consistency.
Derive radiative-transfer and stellar-structure equations, numerically solve bounded stellar models and calculate degenerate-star and thin-disk accretion limits.

practice: Solve a stellar boundary problem and fit a bounded cosmological dataset with explicit model and selection checks.

includes: Automated acquisition, lock-in detection, instrument response, weighted inference and systematic-error validation.

outcomes.description: Automate an optical, electrical or modern-physics experiment and implement DFT and lock-in processing with calibration, timing and noise checks.
Estimate physical parameters with weighted fits and response matrices and test drift, systematic errors, identifiability and alternative physical models.

practice: Complete a spectroscopy or low-noise sensing investigation with acquisition code and an independently challenged uncertainty budget.

includes: Correlations, Landau-Ginzburg models, Monte Carlo, critical phenomena, finite-size scaling and renormalization.

outcomes.description: Calculate Gaussian and mean-field correlations and response and implement Metropolis sampling with detailed-balance, equilibration and autocorrelation diagnostics.
Perform real-space coarse graining and elementary renormalization calculations and compare critical exponents with finite-size simulation evidence.

practice: Implement a lattice Monte Carlo study with autocorrelation-aware errors and finite-size scaling.

includes: Variational calculus, constraints, Lagrangian and Hamiltonian mechanics, symmetries and normal modes.

outcomes.description: Derive conserved quantities from symmetries, calculate Poisson brackets and solve generalized eigenvalue problems for coupled small oscillations.
Derive Euler-Lagrange equations from stationary action, handle holonomic constraints and construct Hamiltonians and canonical equations.

practice: Analyze a constrained coupled system in Lagrangian and Hamiltonian representations.

includes: Stellar equilibrium and evolution, orbital mass inference, galaxies and introductory cosmological models.

outcomes.description: Infer orbital and galactic masses and derive bounded Newtonian expansion and redshift-distance models; evaluate dark-matter and expansion evidence and degeneracies.
Derive hydrostatic and energy-balance stellar equations and apply explicitly taught opacity, blackbody and nuclear-energy scalings to stellar evolution.

practice: Infer stellar or galactic parameters and compare physically distinct models against observational constraints.

includes: Atomic and molecular spectra, selection rules, broadening, two-level dynamics, laser rates and coherent interaction.

outcomes.description: Solve two-level and laser-rate models and infer parameters from resonance, absorption and fluorescence with homogeneous and inhomogeneous broadening.
Calculate fine-structure and external-field shifts, rotational and vibrational spectra and dipole selection rules at introductory perturbative depth.

practice: Assign a spectrum and analyze resonance dynamics with instrumental-width and population checks.

includes: Crystal and reciprocal lattices, diffraction, phonons, bands, transport, semiconductors, magnetism and superconductivity.

outcomes.description: Construct reciprocal lattices and calculate diffraction, one-dimensional phonon and tight-binding dispersions, density of states and band filling.
Calculate bounded carrier and transport models and compare magnetic and superconducting explanations of heat-capacity, susceptibility and conductivity evidence.

practice: Infer a material model from diffraction and transport and propose a discriminating measurement.

includes: Continuum kinematics, stress, strain, fluid and elastic balances, constitutive laws and canonical solutions.

outcomes.description: Construct velocity, strain and stress tensors and derive mass and momentum balances for Newtonian fluids and linear elastic solids.
Solve hydrostatic, Couette, Poiseuille, elementary elastic and linear-wave problems and use dimensionless groups to justify regimes and limitations.

practice: Derive a flow or deformation prediction from balances and test its breakdown against data.

includes: Feedback, transfer functions, frequency response, PID control, controllability, observability and observers.

outcomes.description: Derive mechanical transfer functions and design PID control using poles, frequency response and explicit stability and performance tests.
Construct state-space models, test controllability and observability and calculate pole-placement feedback and observers for small linear systems.

practice: Compare tracking, disturbance rejection and parameter robustness for an oscillator controller.

includes: Electric and magnetic fields, potential, symmetry laws, circuit networks, induction and simple transients.

outcomes.description: Solve circuit networks, derive and solve RC and RL transients by separation and calculate induction, field energy and sinusoidal complex impedance.
Calculate fields and potentials by superposition and symmetry-based Gauss and Ampere laws for line, plane, spherical and cylindrical configurations.

practice: Predict circuit transients and induced voltage and compare calculations with measured traces.

includes: Boundary-value fields, Green functions, multipoles, material response, Maxwell waves and radiation.

outcomes.description: Solve potential boundary problems with images, separation and Green functions and calculate multipoles and dielectric or magnetic response.
Derive Maxwell wave and energy equations and calculate reflection, guided modes, retarded potentials and dipole radiation.

practice: Solve a field boundary and radiating-source problem with energy, dimension and boundary checks.

includes: Diodes, transistor and op-amp models, analog filters, logic, digitization, sampling and discrete Fourier analysis.

outcomes.description: Use explicitly taught diode, transistor and op-amp models to design rectifiers, amplifiers and filters; construct bounded logic and sensor interfaces.
Calculate transfer functions and noise budgets and use supplied DFT tools to diagnose sampling, aliasing, bandwidth and digitizer limits.

practice: Build a low-voltage sensor amplifier and characterize gain, noise, bandwidth and saturation.

includes: Calibration, resolution, sensors, uncertainty, controlled measurement, residual analysis and laboratory decisions.

outcomes.description: Design experiments, propagate uncertainty with explicitly derived finite-difference sensitivity rules and justify changes from residual, risk and data-integrity evidence.
Calibrate length, time, temperature and low-voltage measurements and distinguish resolution, bias, drift and random variation.

practice: Complete a calibration and model test with raw records, an uncertainty budget and justified safety choices.

includes: Stress-energy, Einstein equations, geodesics, black-hole observables, linearized waves and homogeneous cosmology.

outcomes.description: Construct spacetime and stress-energy tensors and derive geodesic and Einstein equations with covariance and conservation identities.
Calculate Schwarzschild redshift, orbital and deflection observables and derive linearized waves and FLRW evolution with explicit coordinate and approximation choices.

practice: Derive an observable prediction from a metric and separate coordinate artifacts from invariant results.

includes: Angular-momentum addition, identical particles, second quantization, scattering, mixed states, open systems and path integrals.

outcomes.description: Add angular momenta and construct symmetrized states and creation-annihilation operators for bounded bosonic and fermionic systems.
Analyze density operators, entanglement and elementary master equations and derive time-sliced path integrals and stationary-action limits.
Derive partial-wave and Born scattering amplitudes and time-ordered perturbative transitions with validity checks.

practice: Solve composite, scattering and dissipative problems in state, operator and propagator representations.

includes: Phase-space distributions, Boltzmann and Vlasov equations, collision operators, transport coefficients and kinetic plasma response.

outcomes.description: Construct phase-space distributions and derive Boltzmann and Vlasov equations and moment balances; prove bounded collision-invariant and entropy-production results.
Calculate diffusion, viscosity and thermal conduction in relaxation-time models and derive linear kinetic plasma response and Landau damping with contour prescriptions.

practice: Compare kinetic and fluid predictions for relaxation and wave damping and identify the closure failure.

includes: Calculus-based particle motion, Newtonian forces, momentum, energy, rigid rotation and elementary gravitation.

outcomes.description: Derive Cartesian and polar particle equations and solve variable-force and constrained-motion cases by integration, separation and conservation.
Calculate centers of mass, moments of inertia, torque and angular momentum and derive elementary central-force and orbital results.

practice: Analyze a rotating assembly and orbit and verify coordinate equations against conservation laws.

includes: Lorentz kinematics, relativistic energy and momentum, photons, matter waves and elementary quantum evidence.

outcomes.description: Calculate photoelectric, Compton, matter-wave and atomic-model predictions and interpret discrete probabilities and continuous measurement densities.
Apply Lorentz transformations and invariant intervals and calculate energy, momentum and elementary reaction thresholds.

practice: Identify experimental observations that distinguish classical, relativistic and quantum predictions.

includes: Hamiltonian nonlinear dynamics, stochastic differential models, Langevin and Fokker-Planck descriptions and relaxation.

outcomes.description: Analyze Hamiltonian resonances and driven nonlinear oscillators with phase-space sections and distinguish transport, regular islands and chaotic dynamics.
Derive bounded Langevin and Fokker-Planck models from drift and diffusion moments and implement Euler-Maruyama with explicit Gaussian sampling and stationary-law checks.

practice: Compare deterministic transport and noisy bistable relaxation with timestep and long-time statistical checks.

includes: Nuclear binding, decay, reactions, scattering, particle classification, conservation laws and detector inference.

outcomes.description: Calculate binding, decay-chain, reaction-threshold and cross-section examples and compare liquid-drop, shell and tunneling models.
Classify particles and interactions, reconstruct invariant masses and interpret detector signals with efficiency, background and counting uncertainty.

practice: Reconstruct a resonance or decay process and separate signal from acceptance and background effects.

includes: Sky coordinates, observing plans, detector calibration, photometry, spectra, parallax and source-selection effects.

outcomes.description: Plan observations in sky coordinates and reduce images using bias, dark and flat corrections; measure aperture flux and background uncertainty.
Apply explicitly defined magnitude, inverse-square, parallax, spectral-line and Doppler relations to estimate source properties and diagnose extinction and selection bias.

practice: Reduce public images or spectra and recover a distance or variable-source signal with calibration checks.

includes: Idealization, dimensions, elementary measurement, algebraic kinematics, forces, energy and momentum.

outcomes.description: Solve constant-acceleration, static-force, work-energy and one-dimensional collision problems with free-body diagrams and conservation laws.
Choose system boundaries, estimate scales, propagate simple bounds and compare dimensional predictions with plotted measurements.

practice: Extract motion from video coordinates and test force and energy explanations.

includes: Gyromotion, drifts, screening, plasma frequency, two-fluid waves and ideal magnetohydrodynamics.
excludes: Kinetic damping is taught in Kinetic Theory.

outcomes.description: Calculate gyromotion and force drifts and derive Debye screening and plasma frequency with characteristic-scale and regime checks.
Derive two-fluid and ideal-MHD balances and linearize plane waves to calculate electrostatic and Alfven dispersion and elementary stability conditions.

practice: Compare confinement and wave scales for a laboratory or space plasma and identify fluid-model limitations.

includes: Relativistic fields, scalar and spinor quantization, gauge symmetry, propagators, diagrams and introductory renormalization.

outcomes.description: Derive propagators and diagram rules and calculate tree amplitudes and regulated scalar one-loop integrals, including contour prescriptions, counterterms and running parameters.
Derive field Euler-Lagrange and Noether relations and quantize scalar and Dirac fields using explicitly developed gamma matrices and gauge constraints.

practice: Compute a scattering cross section and regulated loop correction with symmetry and regulator checks.

includes: State vectors, operators, measurement, finite-state dynamics and one-dimensional Schrodinger problems.
excludes: Three-dimensional angular momentum and general perturbation theory.

outcomes.description: Solve one-dimensional wells, oscillator eigenstates and barrier scattering with matching and normalization; calculate tunneling and probability current.
Normalize state vectors and wavefunctions, calculate probabilities and expectations and evolve finite-state systems with Hermitian Hamiltonians.

practice: Compare matrix and wavefunction predictions and verify a barrier solution's flux conservation.

includes: Interacting lattice Hamiltonians, exact diagonalization, correlations, Berry phases and elementary topological bands.

outcomes.description: Construct occupation-basis lattice Hamiltonians and use tested eigensolver libraries to calculate spectra, correlations and Berry phases in elementary band models.
Use symmetry, finite-size and parameter sweeps to distinguish phase evidence from artifacts and propose measurable and falsifying signatures.

practice: Reproduce a finite-lattice phase diagnostic with basis, size and convergence limitations.

includes: Angular momentum, three-dimensional central potentials, hydrogen, spin and quantum approximation methods.

outcomes.description: Derive angular-momentum commutators and ladders, separate the three-dimensional central-potential equation and calculate hydrogen and spin-one-half observables.
Apply variational, stationary and time-dependent perturbation methods and WKB matching to estimate energies and transition probabilities with validity checks.

practice: Derive spatial spectra and compare perturbative, variational and semiclassical approximations.

includes: Equilibrium ensembles, partition functions, fluctuations, classical and quantum gases and elementary phase transitions.

outcomes.description: Derive microcanonical, canonical and grand-canonical distributions and calculate partition functions, potentials, response and fluctuations.
Derive Bose and Fermi occupations and calculate ideal quantum-gas and elementary spin or mean-field transition predictions.

practice: Compare finite and thermodynamic-limit predictions for a gas and a lattice model.

includes: Temperature, heat, work, thermal laws, entropy, cycles, phase equilibrium and elementary heat transfer.

outcomes.description: Calculate entropy and equilibrium criteria and solve bounded conduction, convection and radiation balances using explicit constitutive models.
Calculate heat, work and internal-energy changes along thermodynamic paths and evaluate calorimetry, engines and refrigerators.

practice: Compare reversible and irreversible processes and quantify heat-transfer device losses.

includes: Oscillations, damping, resonance, traveling and standing waves, acoustics, ray optics, diffraction and polarization.

outcomes.description: Construct ray images and calculate lens, slit, grating and polarization patterns using phase differences and explicitly derived scalar superposition integrals.
Derive harmonic and driven responses using exponential or sinusoidal trials and calculate standing waves, acoustic intensity, interference and Doppler shifts.

practice: Design an acoustic or optical measurement and predict damping, wavelength and finite-resolution effects.
